answer: Ration berths at a wharf: identities cap at 256 non-transferable leases sold by weekly sealed-bid uniform-price auction; winners pay the clearing price, and leases expire after 12 epochs, forcing repricing. Validators verify at payout that claimers hold a live lease. A plume of clones cannot dock: demand above 256 lifts the k-th bid, so n clones pay at least price x n, a linear marginal cost. A shale-thick stack of pre-farmed ids cannot amortize: fee is price x (1 + lease_age/12), aging seats cost more. Attackers cannot split, reset, or pre-farm the fixed berth supply.
